utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Please be seated. Registrar, have the accused brought in. The witness, that is. (The accused/witness entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Good afternoon to the interpreters. Is everybody in his or her seat? Good afternoon. Good afternoon to the Office of the Prosecutor, to Defence counsel, to our witness. I think we also have to say good afternoon to our new registrar who is here, and we would like to welcome her. Are you ready, General Blaskic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. President, Your Honours. Yes, I am, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, let me remind you that the hourglass is still running. I think you have about four or five days left. Is it four, three, two? How many is it?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Well, up to this point the cross-examination has lasted for 9 days and 70 minutes, and the examination-in-chief lasted for longer than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I'd like you to concentrate and try to refer to all of the things that are in support of your -- the charges that you've brought. You are the ones who brought the charges, not the Judges. The Judges support neither the Prosecution or the Defence but are here to judge. Having made these recommendations, let me ask the witness, who is not an accused here, he is a witness. I'm saying this for the public. The witness, pursuant to his obligation, must answer as the Judges have asked, that is, concisely and as clearly as possible, because time is running and I think Sub-rule 90(G) says that the Judges are here to avoid any useless waste of the time. Having said this, like a good father in a family, I say to you, Mr. Kehoe, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good afternoon, Mr. President, Your Honours, counsel. Good afternoon, General.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Kehoe:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, you told us, during your direct testimony, that you need approximately 48 hours to prepare for the commencement of combat operations. With that in mind, General, I ask you when you first began troop movements on the 15th of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Could you ask me in more concrete terms? What troops do you have in mind? There was no troop movement, in fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So on the 15th of April there were no troop movements, according to your testimony, by -- HVO troop movements?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The army, the HVO, on the 15th of April, was still in their houses, that is to say, the HVO did reside in their own homes and so there was no troop movement on the 15th of April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me read you some testimony of Mr. Sulejman Kavazovic, and that is at page 2305, and he notes -- excuse me. It begins on 2306 and my colleague, Mr. Harmon, asks on line 16: "Q Mr. Kavazovic, I would like to turn your attention to the 15th of April and focusing your attention on that date." Moving down to line 23 the question is: "Q After you finished your work, and this is the 15th, where did you go? A When I finished work at 3:10, I headed for my house where I was living." On the next page at line 1 on 2307: "A Along the route I noticed that the situation in town was unusual. There seemed to be no civilians. There were groups of the HVO of two to three soldiers in combat gear standing next to buildings, and I thought it was rather strange. So I concluded that the situation was not good. There were no civilians, obviously." Line 20 on that same page: "Q Mr. Kavazovic, after you returned to your house, what did you do? A I checked to see whether my wife was there. However, my wife was with her parents at their apartment. So I went in the direction of my in-law's apartment to see my wife, and passing through the park, I saw three or four groups of six to seven soldiers, each running in the direction of the hotel. Q How were these soldiers dressed? A They were in full combat gear. They had camouflage uniforms, helmets on their heads, and automatic rifles." Turning to the following page, on 2309, line 4: "A I was moving from my house through this park and from this direction ..." And he indicates on the map the town of Vitez. "... from the centre of town. There were three or four groups of six to seven soldiers, each running towards the hotel from the park. They were running through the park in the direction of the Hotel Vitez. Q Approximately what time of day was that? A It was maybe 3.50 or 4.00 in the afternoon." Moving down to line 16: "A Yes, they were running. Yes, that is true. They were running in the direction of the Hotel Vitez. They were running along here and they were going towards the centre, the part where the hotel is." Now, let me read you the testimony of Witness G who lives in Ahmici, on the road between Busovaca and Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Witness G was a protected witness, Mr. President, who testified in open. This is on page 3852. "Q How far was your house from the main road that went from Vitez into Busovaca? A About a hundred metres, perhaps. Q On the 15th of April, were you at home? A Yes. Q Who normally lived with you at that house? A I lived with my mother, my father, and my sister. Q On 15 April, did you see anything unusual at home? A Yes. I could notice that along the main road an increased number of HVO vans with clearly-marked signs of the HVO. Q Where were they going, what direction? A They were going into both directions, both toward Vitez and Busovaca. They were simply moving along. Q What was unusual about those vans? A There were many people in there and they were all in uniforms. They were not civilians, so that was a little unusual to me." So, General, there were, in fact, increased troop movements during the 15th of April, 1993, weren't there?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. You asked me about increased troop movements, that is to say, whether the brigades, battalions, companies, and platoons were moving on orders. The witness was speaking about the movement of groups of soldiers, two to three soldiers, in front of the park towards the hotel --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Reformulate your question, please. Rephrase it so the witness can answer it specifically, otherwise, we'll be playing with words. "Troop movements" or "troops moving around"? Be very, very specific, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you order troops to move during the day on the 15th of April, 1993, "Yes" or "No"?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I did not order troops to move during the day on April 15, 1993, and there was no troop movement. It was the comment that you read out, probably referring to the moving about of soldiers to ensure security for the Hotel Vitez. There was a regular group of 20 or so military policemen in front of that building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Movements. All right. There were movements of military personnel, HVO, who were in charge of ensuring -- they were guarding over Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, the 15th of April was the expiration day for yet another unilateral order by the HVO to force the ABiH at cantons 3, 8, and 10 to subordinate themselves to the HVO; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That is not so, because I never received an order in that sense. The only order that I received was the order from the chief of the main staff from January 1993, linked to the attachment of the units of the BH army and the HVO, but I did not receive orders of that kind on the 15th of April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let us turn our attention to Prosecutor's Exhibit 25, if we can. It was next on that list. This, as you may recall, Mr. President, is the newspaper article from Slobodna Dalmacija regarding a press release of the HVO concerning the implementation of the Vance-Owen Plan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Well, you have a great deal of confidence in our memories to say that we would remember Prosecution Exhibit 25. That goes back quite awhile.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I suppose it does, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. Thank you, Mr. Registrar. We have the exhibit, that is, Prosecution Exhibit 25. Let me give it to my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I do believe there are French and English copies of these.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, this particular article is written by Veso Vegar, who is the press information officer for the HVO in Mostar; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: For a time -- that is to say, it says here an officer of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna for information. I know that at one time he was the Porte-parole in the ITD, the information and propaganda activity of the HVO. Now, when he performed what duty, I can't really say. I haven't got any data on that because he was in Mostar and not in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, pursuant to the order that was issued by the HVO on the 3rd of April, 1993, the HVO ordered the following in number 2: "2. All armed forces of the HVO and the police of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, as well as the BH army and the BH Ministry of Defence, which originate outside the provinces, shall have to identify themselves and leave such provinces within three days. "3. Until the complete demilitarisation of Bosnia-Herzegovina, as envisioned under the peace plan and for reasons of a more efficient defence against aggression, the domicile forces of the HVO and the BH army in provinces 1, 5, and 9 shall be placed under the command of the main staff of the BH army, and provinces 3, 8, and 10 under the command of the main staff of the HVO. "Those forces which cannot accept this decision shall have a possibility to leave the provinces. "4. Main staff of the HVO and the main staff of the BH army shall set up a joint command no later than 15 April, 1993." Let us move down to the next two full paragraphs after 6. "The HVO of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna hopes that Izetbegovic, having understood the exceptional importance of the statement, will sign that document as well, because the document also confirms the desire for peace which is so necessary for everyone. "In the event that the statement is not signed by the heads of the Muslim delegation in provinces 3, 8, and 10, the HVO of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna has decided to apply the provisions of the peace plan where each national armed force will have to withdraw to its domicile province." Once again, General, we see a unilateral ultimatum by the HVO demanding that BiH troops subordinate themselves to the HVO by 15 April, 1993 or the HVO would unilaterally implement that subordination?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I did not have a chance of reading the document when it was published because I didn't have these press clippings. May I just have a moment to read through it? Because I think that Mr. Veso Vegar refers back to a meeting of the civilian authorities. So if I may have some time to read through the document, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, briefly, before you read the document, General, this document was read at the 13 April, 1993 press conference that you attended with Dario Kordic where Dario Kordic read this document, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't remember him reading that document. It is possible. All I'm saying is that I didn't have the document in my own hands and that I did not read it before. I see this document for the first time here in the courtroom. I don't remember whether Dario Kordic read it or not. If you say he did, then probably he did. But could I just have a look and read through it, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Was this disclosed to the Defence, this exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This particular document came into evidence at the end of June 1997. I hate to bring up that date so far away, but it's been in evidence for quite some time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Hayman, I think that your client had the opportunity to look through this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: As has Your Honours, but it's impossible to keep all these documents in one's mind, Mr. President. It's impossible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Yes, you're right, absolutely right, but that will give me the opportunity to give the witness a little less time in order to familiarise himself with the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I might add, to expedite matters, have the witness take a look at this at the break, and I will reserve questions on this exhibit until thereafter so we can move this along.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I think that you can ask your question now. General Blaskic, I think you should have had enough time to familiarise yourself with the document. I would like the Prosecutor to ask his questions. Mr. Kehoe, please ask your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, there was a unilateral plan by the HVO to implement the Vance-Owen Plan, and the expiration date for that unilateral plan was 15 April, 1993; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know about any plan of that kind. I was not aware of a plan like that, nor did I receive instructions concerning that kind of plan. In this document, we're talking about a government meeting, that is to say, a meeting of the civilian authorities, and in document number 25, the civilian authorities --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I think you've explained the distinction. You said that you were the military individual, they were civilians, and that the military people don't know what the civilians are doing and the civilians don't know what the military people are doing. I think you've already answered that question and it's been noted.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I should just like to add one more word, if I may. Not even on the 15th of April --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, but do it quickly, please.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That is to say, not even on the 15th of January when a number of orders on attachment were brought in, in Central Bosnia, I did not even try to implement them because it was unrealistic, whereas now in April when I had six enclaves, it was even more unrealistic, so that the HVO was not capable of even giving thought to trying to implement an order of that kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us turn to the next document, if I can, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is Prosecution Exhibit 687 and 687A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, this is an order coming from the vice-president of the HVO of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, Anto Valenta, on the 14th of April, 1993 to all the presidents of the municipalities in Central Bosnia, and the order is: "Because of the intensified tensions following a number of incidents in the majority of the municipalities in Central Herceg-Bosna and the deterioration of the situation, I hereby order: "A curfew to be imposed in all municipalities in Central Herceg-Bosna from 2100 to 0600 hours and catering establishments not to remain open after 2000 hours. "The schools will cease working until Monday 19 April 1993, after which an assessment will be made and a decision will be reached about whether to continue work. "This order takes place immediately." Now, in conjunction with this particular document, I'd like to read some testimony to you, General, before I ask my question. This is the --

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Counsel, I apologise for interrupting. I'm confused, Mr. President, because the original has the 15th of April on it and the English translation is dated the 14th of April. So does counsel know what the date of this was? Of course, the Totic kidnapping was the morning of the 14th and not the 15th, so perhaps counsel can help us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, counsel. I just take the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Do we think that this was authored on the 15th?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I believe this is a translation of what I have here, counsel. I have no reason to believe otherwise, other than the transcription may be incorrect.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Maybe we can also get this stamp down at the bottom of the document which hasn't been translated, Mr. President, which also appears to have the 15th of April as some kind of transmission or receipt date. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hayman. Perhaps we don't need the translation service to see that it's the 15th rather than the 14th of April. Would that change the sense of your question, Mr. Kehoe?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It doesn't, Judge, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: It doesn't change the sense of the question. But having said that, we will do as you like, Mr. Hayman, and will have the seal translated, the seal at the bottom of the page, unless the interpreters could do it immediately which would avoid having to call upon the translation service. Do you have the seal on the ELMO? We could put it in Serbo-Croat on the ELMO and ask the interpreters to interpret it quickly. The seal right under the signature of Anto Valenta.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Mr. Nobilo can read it, if that's convenient, Mr. President. The other thing, could we pen in the correct date on the English translation so that the exhibit is correct? Otherwise, I'm concerned that at the end of the case, in final argument when referring to exhibits, we may all get confused because we won't remember these errors unless we actually make the change.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I agree, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely. I agree as well. Mr. Nobilo, please read the seal, and the interpreters will interpret it quickly for us, under the seal of Anto Valenta.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The first line, it says: "Name of body of HVO," and then we have the letters "TRA" within the stamp, and then written in handwriting is the letters "CV." Under that, it says, "Transmitted and received, reference number 06/11971," and then the figure was written in hand. The third line says "Day," and then in handwriting, "15 April," then "09," and then there's a comma and another 9 written in by hand, "in" and then the hour, "o'clock." Under that "TLP," an abbreviation, and it says "TB, packet, RV, ZV, RAV, RV, TLP." Those are the abbreviations of certain resources or means. General Blaskic will be able to tell us more. Then it says "Processed," and in hand it says, "Vesna Stojak."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, will you tell the translation service that the date was April 15th and not the 14th? But at times, that can be important. I don't think that changes very much in respect of your question, Mr. Prosecutor, so you can continue. Thank you, Mr. Hayman.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me proceed with the testimony of Adnan Zec on page 4273, beginning with the question on line 24: "Q What, if anything, unusual did you notice when you went to school on 15th April? A Yes, I noticed that certain Croatian children, children of the Croatian extraction, were not attending school, especially the children from Ahmici." Moving ahead to 4276, the witness notes, this is again Adnan Zec, on the 4th: "A Yes, when I returned, my parents were commenting on why these children from Ahmici did not go to school that day. They saw them around on that day. Then the Milicevic family, these are three households, three families, they had driven their families away in cars, and in front of Ivo Papic's house, different vehicles were constantly coming and going. Q The Milicevic family is Croat and the Papic family you mentioned are also Croats; is that correct? A Yes." So it would appear, General, based on the testimony that we have, that the people in Ahmici at least believe that something is about to happen that would cause them to move their families out of the area; isn't that right, sir?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, from this document that you gave, 687, it is certain that there were high tensions. This is an order by the civilian authorities that were sent to the presidents of the civilian municipalities. I don't recall having seen this kind of a document at all because I wasn't in charge of regulating the school year and when children would go to school and when they would not go to school. However, many incidents happened, and they probably made the author of the document decide on this, and obviously this was sent to the centre in Travnik, the communications centre of Travnik, not the communications centre of the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia. I just want to say briefly that we should recall these incidents in Travnik on the 8th of April and in Novi Travnik on the 13th of April where officers from the brigade from Novi Travnik were abducted by the Mujahedin, and then on the 13th of April in the Frankopan Brigade when an entire shift of soldiers was taken prisoner by the BH army, and an attempt was made to kill Mr. Ilija Nakic, commander of the brigade, and his driver was killed. Then on the 12th of April, in the town of Vitez, two officers from the Vitez Brigade were taken prisoner, and the killing of Darko Kraljevic was attempted on the 13th of April, and then Zivko Totic was kidnapped in a terrorist manner on the 15th of April, and all of Zenica was blocked. In addition to that, a bomb was thrown in Zenica, and six children were killed by the 314th Motorised Brigade of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina from the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: There were many incidents, and tensions were running high, and schools were not working. But I wish to point out that the orders of the civilian authorities are not binding on me as a military commander, and I do not recall having received this document at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, General, what orders from Milivoj Petkovic did you get on the 15th to take actions with your troops? Did you get any?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I informed the chief of the main staff about the incident, about practically all the incidents, including the incident that occurred in Zenica --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me, General. I'm going to cut you off here. What orders did you get from Milivoj Petkovic to move your troops anywhere on the 15th of April? That's the question. Did you get that order? If my question wasn't clear before, that's the question I want to ask you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: General, answer the question precisely, please, specifically, please.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The order I received on the 15th of April from General Petkovic said that after all the terrorist actions, if the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina launches an all-out attack against the HVO, then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I'm not getting any interpretation. I am just reading it here, but I didn't get interpretation. Yes, it's coming through now. There seems to be a problem in the booth. I hope I didn't insult you. I didn't mean to. I just wasn't hearing the interpretation, even though I was able to read what was on the monitor. But the sentence was not finished.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: May I proceed, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, please continue.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: So the order was that the forces of the military police and the Vitezovi were being attached to me and that I should organise the blockade and protection of villages from this all-out attack by the BH army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the only order you received?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, that was the only order that I received from the chief of the main staff of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me show you another document, General.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is Prosecution Exhibit 688, 688A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, this is an order from Milivoj Petkovic directed to you on the 15th of April, 1993, marked "Urgent, Urgent, Urgent." It notes as follows: "In view of the newly created situation in the region of Konjic municipality and the difficult position of the Herceg Stjepan Brigade, I here order: "1. A part of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone forces shall be used to tie down the BH army forces as follows: "- Re-enforce a part of forces from Fojnica to Pozetva in the south-east Herzegovina zone of responsibility and thus link up with the northern part of Klis. "- With part of the forces in Kiseljak and Kresevo to prevent the infiltration of fresh forces from Bosnia and link up with Bradina, Repovci, Stojkovici, and Gobelovina, deadline immediately. "3. Due to the importance of the order, you shall report to me on its execution in writing." Now, General, this was a very urgent order sent to you by Milivoj Petkovic for you to take action immediately on the 15th of April, 1993. Now, other than this order, did you receive any other orders from Milivoj Petkovic for you to deploy your troops?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: First of all, in connection with this order, I see that this order also has a stamp of the main staff of the HVO and that it was issued, but it doesn't have the stamp that was usually there that I received it, so I'm not sure as to whether I received it or not. I did not take any action related to assistance except for taking in civilians that were withdrawing from Pozetva, and I know that the HVO units could not help Pozetva and Fojnica. I remember, and I have this noted, that I received an order from General Petkovic on the 15th of April and I testified about that, but all the orders that arrived I did not note. I mean, I did not register them. They were registered in the registry service.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: But in principle, you received it; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. President, I do not recall. Perhaps I did, but I'm surprised that there is not a stamp saying that I received it, because all the orders that I received would have to have a seal that it was received. There is a stamp here saying that it was issued -- that this order was issued at the main staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: That's your answer, simply that there's no seal, and the Judges will evaluate this as they see fit. Please move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, for the record, this document was received from the Croatian side of the federation and it was delivered to Lieutenant-Colonel Jean-Pierre Capelle, retired, of the French army, who is now on the staff of the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, did you ignore this order?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Perhaps another question, General Blaskic, as my colleague has just pointed out to me. It says "Urgent" three times. Do you remember other orders that say "Urgent, Urgent, Urgent" on it? Do you remember? "Yes" or "No"? It's possible, when the document has the order "Urgent" on it three times, you may not be particularly struck by it. Quickly, please. Quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Mr. President, with the translation, it's not possible to answer that quickly. I would please ask the Court to show patience when you're urging the witness, "Quickly, quickly, quickly," in a foreign language. It takes some time to be translated so that he can hear the question, and answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hayman. I should have remembered my responsibility to try to keep in mind there is interpretation here. When an order is received on the 15th of April at a time when there was all this tension that you've spoken about -- you've remembered very well. You have a very clear memory. You remembered a little while ago all the incidents that happened on the 15th of April. When you have an order from General Petkovic which is marked "Urgent" three times, do you remember that or don't you?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I said, Mr. President, that it is quite possible that this document arrived. I'm not precluding that possibility, but I'm sure that no action was taken in accordance with this document and point 1 was not adhered to. I'm sure of that, because on the 15th of April we had lots of problems ourselves. I had lots of problems on the 15th and I was not in a position to help someone else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do with the order?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I already said that it is possible that this order was received, but I'm surprised there was no stamp on it. If it was received, then I certainly informed them about the overall situation, that is say, I informed the chief of the main staff. In the Lasva pocket, the situation was highly tense and complex, and there were a great many incidents, and I was not in a position to give anybody help because I needed help myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Let me speak slowly. When you receive an order marked "Urgent, Urgent, Urgent," you just don't send -- I suppose that you would inform General Petkovic of what was going on. As the commander in chief you received -- I can understand that you didn't receive it, but if you received it, would you send him back a letter informing him of the situation or would you carry out the order?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have to certainly take this order into account, and if I received it, then certainly when I had this telephone conversation with General Petkovic, I informed him about the situation on my side, and I believed that when he wrote this order he did not have all information as to what was going on in my environment but, of course, I could not turn a deaf ear to the order as if I had never received it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, this order would have the effect of preventing the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina of resupplying and moving troops further into Central Bosnia; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Allow me to read this first, please. This order was sent in order to have help delivered to the HVO of the municipality of Konjic, primarily to reinforce the village of Pozetva, which was about to fall. Croats were fleeing from there towards Fojnica and Kiseljak. This second section that says that part of the forces from Kiseljak and Kresevo could prevent the infiltration of fresh forces from Bosnia towards Konjic, because the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina at that time was launching an initiative against Konjic, and the HVO was encircled, and the HVO army was expelled from the municipality of Konjic around the 15th of April, 1993. This is actually the end of the total encirclement of the HVO of Central Bosnia through the municipalities of Konjic and Gornji Vakuf by the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, General, let's move on to these discussions with Petkovic. You told us at 15.00 that Petkovic told you that in view of an all-out attack or if there were an all-out attack by the ABiH, the Vitezovi and the military police would be attached to you. Now, you received information during your meeting at 17.00 with Pasko Ljubicic, and Darko Kraljevic, and Zuti, and others that there were ABiH troop movements on Kuber. Do you recall that testimony, sir?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I received information that forces of the BH army were on the move towards Kuber, but during the latter half of the meeting I think that Pasko Ljubicic was present and the commander of Vitezovi, Darko Kraljevic, was present too, and the commander from the Tvrtko special purpose unit was present as well. During the second half of the meeting, I think that Zuti was not present, to the best of my recollection.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, this information alarmed you and caused you to read out the orders that you had issued, Exhibit 267 and 268; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it would be fair to say that you reacted to this information concerning these Bosnian army troop movements almost immediately, as a good commander would?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The situation was such that I had to react to such information and that is what I did in order to prevent the possibility of any surprise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, during this meeting, did you tell Pasko Ljubicic and Darko Kraljevic that in the event of an all-out attack, Petkovic had told you that they were going to be attached to them? Did you tell him that information?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At this meeting, I read the orders out to them in case of an all-out attack and I spelled out precisely what their tasks were. As far as I can remember, they did not ask me specifically about this activity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, please. The question I ask you is: Did you tell them during this meeting that you had spoken to Petkovic four hours before and that in the event of an all-out attack, the Vitezovi and the military police were going to be attached to you? Did you tell them that during the meeting, "Yes" or "No"?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I talk to them about the overall situation, and earlier on Darko Kraljevic told me that he was at the disposal, and I said that I had talked to the chief of the main staff, and I said what the position of the chief of the main staff was in case the BH army attacked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How about the military police? Did you tell Pasko Ljubicic that Petkovic had said that in the event of an attack the military police would be attached?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I said that to all the participants in the meeting. Pasko Ljubicic was at the meeting and he could have heard me say that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, at 23.00, General, you receive very significant information concerning combat operations in Kuber. If I might read those to you briefly. They're at page 18502, or if the pagination is wrong, counsel, it would be 18491, but at line 12 in response to Mr. Nobilo's questions you noted as follows: "Around 23.00 I was informed that combat operations were in progress at Kuber and there was shelling from Preocica --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could you please slow down?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I will. I'm sorry. I'll start over from the beginning. Line 12: "At about 23.00, I was informed that combat operations were in progress at Kuber and there was shelling from Preocica in the area of Poculica. I was also informed that at Kuber there were some HVO wounded in the course of the combat operations." In addition to that information, General, you noted for us that the military intelligence group told you that there was a regrouping of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Now, General, with this information that you received at 23.00, did you contact the special purpose units, Vitezovi, Tvrtko, Zuti?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I did not contact these units because at Mount Kuber were the soldiers of the Vitez, Busovaca, and Zenica brigades, respectively. When I talked to Cerkez, commander of the Vitez Brigade, I asked him to inform the members of the Vitez Brigade about movements, troop movements, of the BH army on the 15th of April, 1993, that is to say, to warn them that there was such troop movement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let us clarify that point, General. You talked to Cerkez about the troop movements at Kuber at approximately 18.00, and I am talking to you about the information that you received at 23.00 concerning combat operations at Kuber. My question concerning that information, concerning combat operations, did you contact the special purpose units and did you contact the brigades with this new information?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I did not contact the brigades with this new information because new information came from the brigades, that is to say, that the brigades, in their own system of reporting, sent to my duty officer this information. Now, precisely whether the Vitez Brigade or the Nikola Subic-Zrinjski Brigade sent that information to me, that I do not know exactly, but Kuber is a pretty big mountain and it's quite far away. I don't see any special purpose for this even if I had informed these commanders about this kind of activity. There were also operations against Poculica, not only Kuber. Also, there was a break-off in communications from time to time, but there were such information too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, General, as a prudent commander, wouldn't a prudent commander contact as many people as possible within his organisation to tell them about the onset of combat activities?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, may I just say this, at Kuber, the forces were confronted from January 1993, that is to say, that we never managed to delineate the front line there. If anything would happen, I was receiving information from my subordinates. I did not have my own observer there at Kuber, and there is no point in my informing someone who had already informed me about that. Had I received information from some independent source and in relation to that position, I certainly would have forwarded that kind of information to my commanders so that they could familiarise the soldiers with that, as I did in the case of Mario Cerkez at 18.00, 18.30, whatever, when I told him to warn them that there was troop movement by the BH army from the direction of Zenica towards Kuber. So this was information that I was receiving from them on the ground, and there was nobody else who could have told me there was operations against Kuber other than those soldiers there at Kuber.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, General, did you contact the main staff and tell them about these combat operations in Kuber?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I did not at that time, because there was an exact timetable as to when we sent information to the main staff about all events. If something extraordinary had happened, then we would have to see what this extraordinary thing would turn into, whether this was just one incident or whether these were operations that would go on against Kuber, Poculica and, also, the radio communications, whether they were cut off by the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I could show you a photograph, Prosecution Exhibit 258. If we could put that on the ELMO. Who is that man, General?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That is Vladimir Santic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What position did he have in the military police?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I know that for a certain period of time he was commander of a company of the military police and for a certain period of time he was also acting commander of the battalion of the military police, except that I don't know for sure which periods of time -- when he was commander of the company and when he was acting commander of the battalion of the military police, but I know him in both capacities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, on the 15th of April, 1993, Vladimir Santic had an office in the Hotel Vitez, right down the hall from you, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: He had an office in the Hotel Vitez not only on the 15th of April but before the 15th of April and afterwards at the Hotel Vitez as commander of a company or deputy commander of the battalion of the military police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, General, as a prudent office who knows that the military police is not in the Viteska Brigade chain of command, did you inform Vlado Santic or anybody else in the military police that combat activities had started in Kuber at 23.00 on the evening of the 15th?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I did not contact Vlado Santic. I'm not sure whether he was at the hotel at that time at all. As commander, I was in contact with the commander of the battalion and there was no need for me to establish contact with the commander of a company. It would have been a surprise to me if he would be at the hotel at the time. He lived in the immediate neighbourhood of the hotel and, I believe, I'm not sure, but I believe that he was at his own apartment then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, General, did you contact anybody in the military police, Pasko Ljubicic or anybody else, about this information that you received from Kuber that combat activities had begun at 23.00?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I did not contact the military police, because they do not have something to do with the Kuber position. It was the home guard units that were there, and this was an incident, and we had to wait and see how this activity would develop further at Kuber. I do not see any special reason why I would contact anyone except for those who were at these positions at Kuber.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, General, you had given the military police the responsibility of ensuring that the main road between Vitez and Busovaca was secured, and by that I refer to your order, Defence Exhibit 267; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That was the regular daily task of the military police, and with the order I reminded them of their daily task. It was not a new task assigned to them because it was the basic duty of the military police to ensure the security of the roads, particularly the traffic police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Given that they were to secure that road, by your own terms, that road could only be secured if, and I read your testimony at 18563, that road can only be secured, at line 6: "A ... if you control the high ground and positions and features around it. This is very clear on this model because whoever controls the high ground and features absolutely controls the communication line and traffic, because at any time, with the artillery and with fire, he can cut off the road and prevent traffic." Now, given that there were combat activities in Kuber, according to your testimony, that there was shelling of Croat villages by ABiH, and you believed that the military police had to secure the road from the high ground, you, nonetheless, took no steps to inform the military police of what was happening up in Kuber; is that your testimony, General?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: First, you claim, not me, that there was combat activities. "Combat activities" implies opening fire and the start of fighting, and if there is individual shelling, then it can be for the army to take certain coordinates and it can be due to provocation and so on. So the units did not enter into fighting fully, but there was individual shelling up at Kuber. Once there was fighting, that is to say, that combat activities had started and that there was shooting on both sides, I did not receive that information. All I received was that there was individual shelling going on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, you noted for us again at line 12 of 18491 that: "A About 23.00 hours, I was informed that combat operations were in progress at Kuber and that there was shelling from Preocica in the area of Poculica. I was also informed that at Kuber there were some HVO wounded in the course of the combat operations." Now, General, using your own logic, you know, based on what you've told this Court, if you admit that you contacted the military police after you received this information at 23.00, they would have been attached to you; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I have already said that I received orders that should there be a general all-out attack by the BH army on the HVO positions, that all forces are attached to me, and this is a question of an all-out, general attack. In my testimony, I stated that a general attack, an all-out attack, does not apply -- we see that about 20 positions were in question, not only one position. I already said that I received this information from my subordinates, that is to say, from the Nikola Subic-Zrinjski Brigade or the Vitez Brigade, and that they informed me of events up at Kuber. I did not inform the commander of the military police of this or the other commanders either because I considered that it still was not an all-out, general attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the actions in Kuber where there is shelling and HVO wounded doesn't qualify as an all-out attack for an attachment; is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: An all-out attack on the overall region was undertaken by the BH army on the 16th of April at about 23 positions there, and here we're talking about activities by the BH armies on one position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, would you agree that the reasonably prudent thing for you to do would have been to go to the military police and tell them to take the high ground outside of Ahmici, Nadioci, and Santici in order to protect the road? That would have been the prudent thing to do, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: We were still waiting for the attack. If I were to look at it today, perhaps I would have made different moves. But I had all the intelligence assessments which showed us that there could be an attack, whereas the decision was on the other side, and it would have been a much better thing that there had been no attack and that there were no combat activities launched.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, given the fact that you did not order the military police to immediately take that high ground, that would indicate to a neutral observer that they had another assignment first before they took that high ground outside of Ahmici, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Linked to taking the high ground, well, at those positions, the 3rd Battalion or the 2nd Battalion of the 325th Brigade of the BH army, and had I issued an order to that effect to take the high ground, all the high ground, perhaps that would have caused the beginning of an attack and combat activities in the area. I did everything in my power, truly everything in my power, to avoid the beginning of any kind of conflict because I had six enclaves, and that can be seen from this model here. There is a great gap between Busovaca and Kiseljak, and it was my interest to achieve peace because I was in a disadvantageous position. That is why I issued the order for a blockade and not for the defence, that is to say, the most passive possible self-defence order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, the reality of the situation was they had an assignment in the morning at 5.30 in Ahmici before they took that high ground, and that was based on your instructions, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The question reflects your own opinion too clearly. Please rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, is it true that the military police had an assignment in Ahmici at 5.30 in the morning, and their second assignment was then taking the high ground outside of Ahmici thereafter?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I said exactly what I ordered to the military police and what instructions the members of the military police received from me. I do not know whether there were other activities or not. What I heard here from witnesses, from Prosecution witnesses here at the Tribunal, convinced me that probably some individuals were acting on orders, because in that short space of time, they could not have committed such a great crime with somebody having organised and planned this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, other than the exhibits that we have seen, Exhibits 267, 268, and 269, what other orders did you give to your brigades and independent units prior to 5.30 in the morning on the 16th?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was an order to the Vitez Brigade, I don't know exactly what number, it was issued at 01.30 on the 16th of April, 1993 and refers to the blockade of certain villages in the municipality of Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me show you, General, Prosecutor's Exhibit 521. While we're waiting for that, General, based on your testimony that there was no activity by the military police on the evening of the 15th of April, 1993, where was the front line on the evening of the 15th of April, 1993? Excuse me, General. I'm asking you a question first, and then we'll get to that document. Where was the front line?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know which municipality you mean. If you want me to talk about the entire front line, I can do that too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The front line between Vitez and Zenica. Where was the front line in that area?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In that area, there was only one position at Kuber, and it was called feature Vran Stijena where there was the anti-aircraft defence position previously. I think it was the trigonometry -- I would have to see which elevation it was exactly. That was the position, there was no other position, because the members of the Vitez Brigade had the front line against the Serbian army at the Travnik and Novi Travnik municipality at Strikanci Slatka Vode. That was the position. That was where the soldiers of the Vitez Brigade were located up at the front line, together with the members of the BH army from Travnik and the members of the Travnik HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, let us turn back to Exhibit 521, which is the exhibit identified as being received in the Hotel Vitez by your chief of operations, Slavko Marin, and it is an operation report from the morning of 16 April, 1993 from the Jure Francetic Brigade noting at 06.00: "The night was quiet in the zone covered by the brigade. All units are holding the positions they had seized. The town is under control and our units are letting unarmed civilians who are going to work pass through." When did you issue an order to the Jure Francetic Brigade to seize positions and what positions did they seize?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: First of all, I'd like to say something with regard to this document. It was received by the operative official on duty. It is an operative report sent at 6.00 every morning --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me, General. That's not the question. The question is very simple, and I'll repeat it to you again. When did you issue an order to the Jure Francetic Brigade to seize positions, and what positions did they seize as of this report at 06.00 on the 16th of April?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In document 267, a task was issued, an assignment was issued to all the HVO brigades. It was a preparatory assignment, and point 3 is stipulated to perform defence in the zone of responsibility and to prevent extremist Muslim forces in realising an open clearing up of the area and genocide over the Croatian people and the realisation of their own goals, to be on the alert for a defence of the Croatian people and to withdraw forces only once the people had been evacuated and taken care of and once I give the okay for that. Probably there was self-organisation on the part of the forces after the terrorist act, that is to say, when the commander of the Jure Francetic Brigade was kidnapped, and there were the Croatian villages in the Zenica municipality that were concerned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, you told us during your testimony that you never sent Exhibit 267, the order of the 15th of April at 10.00, you never sent that to the brigades because it hadn't been typed and it had to be sent back to be retyped; do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I remember that the order had not been typed and sent at 17.00 on the 15th of April, 1993, but I do believe that later on, the order was sent. But it was not typed out even later on in April '93, and on the 22nd or 23rd of April, it was typed out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The bottom line, General, is that on the 15th of April of 1993, you never sent out Exhibit 267 to the brigades. Given that information, I ask my question to you again: What positions did they seize and on what orders did the Jure Francetic Brigade seize these positions?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The Jure Francetic Brigade, I already said, had taken up positions in Croatian villages of the Zenica municipality. I believe that that was so, and at this point in time, I cannot remember the number of the order. But quite certainly, after the terrorist act and the seizing of the commander of the Jure Francetic Brigade, the soldiers from the brigade itself became activated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, was it pursuant to an order that you issued, given the fact that you're the commander in chief of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I have already said that I believe that it could have been order 267 because that order refers to the brigade. It was the order that had not been retyped but was written in handwriting and given to Slavko Marin to complete.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Was the order sent or not sent? Could we have that point clarified?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: We will pull the portion of the witness's testimony where he reflects that it was not sent to the brigades. That was the testimony in response to the questions by Mr. Nobilo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. We will have to clarify that later. It has to be clarified, General Blaskic. We have to know exactly whether you sent it or didn't send it and what is the proper statement that you made. I think that we should take a break now to allow everyone to think about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We will now resume the hearing. Please be seated. Mr. Kehoe, you can now continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, with regard to Exhibit 267, I referred Your Honours to a series of pages starting with 18482, with a question by Mr. Nobilo that reads that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I would like the registrar to give us 267. Thank you very much. Yes, you can continue, please, because we remember that exhibit. We saw it yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes. At line 19: "Q So this information came that the BH army from Zenica was on the move from that absolutely pivotal, strategic point in the Lasva Valley. Did this news cause you some concern? A Yes, of course, not the least because the duty officer came and delivered it in a state of near panic, and he delivered it to everybody present. Everybody overheard this and the question immediately arose what to do and what position to take with respect to this action on the part of the BH army. Q And so what was your reaction? Who did you task with following up on this? A At that point I told the participants of the meeting that I had already issued two orders, one that morning and one in the afternoon, and that I expected that these orders would be followed, that is, complied with. I asked Slavko Marin to bring me those orders and I saw then that the preparatory order which I had issued at 10.00 had still not been sent to the subordinate units." This is the meeting at 17.00. Carrying on a few pages to 18485, at line 11, by Mr. Nobilo: "Q You said the order of 10.00 of the 15th of April, 1993 remained in its handwritten form and had not been sent. For purposes of the record, it is document D267. What happened with the order that was D268, the order written on the 15th of April at 3.45? A That order was not sent either. Q What happened next? A I took both these orders and I read them out orally to the commanders present at the meeting. After I had read out the provisions of the order, after I had read them out, we concluded the meeting. I decided after that to call the commander of the Vitez Brigade who was at that time in his family house." On the next page, 18486, at line 6: "A At that particular time I was not able to send the orders out to be typed, the 10.00 order, because the typist wasn't around, wasn't in her office, because according to her regular shift, she was on duty until 3.00. So after that, the order -- the order came later. The 3.45 order was sent out because it had been typed whereas the 10.00 order was returned to the general services office for the typist to type it out, and I read out the assignments from the two orders orally to the individuals present." We had a list of the people who were there and, of course, the Zenica Brigade commander was not at this meeting. There was also a series of -- a conversation in closed session with Your Honours, from page 18951 to 18960, concerning 267 bis, which was the numerical issue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, General, 267 was never sent to the Zenica brigades, was it?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I checked in my notes and that order was not sent to the Zenica Brigade, and I do believe that after the commander of the brigade, Totic, had been seized, the soldiers and command of the brigade organised themselves and raised their combat readiness in their region of deployment, which is an expected reaction of soldiers in that brigade. It could have been expected.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when this individual writes that units are holding positions that they had seized at 06.00, that was done unilaterally by the unit and not ordered by you; is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I have already said that quite possibly they -- that unit organised itself and that I agreed with that. On the 15th of April, I was, in fact, absent from my office for a time and these orders were on the table belonging to the duty officer on duty and perhaps some of the operative officials read it out, but document P21 is a regular report by the duty officer of the Jure Francetic Brigade of Zenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, General, just to compare these two situations, when you received this information from the officer on duty at 17.00 about the movement of troops, when he's near panic, you take immediate steps --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Please speak slowly, Mr. Prosecutor. The interpreters are having difficulty following you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, ladies and gentlemen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, when we look at these two situations, you receive information about troop movements at 17.00, you react immediately, yet when you receive information at 23.00 about combat operations in Kuber, you do nothing. Would that be a fair assessment of these two situations?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It is not a good assessment because it is not true that I did nothing concerning Kuber. I received the information as to what was going on at Kuber, and I endeavoured to attend to the developments there. That was perhaps just one incident where a soldier was wounded and not an all-out attack. Throughout that time, I tried to avoid, as I say, an all-out attack and a general conflict. Let me also say, with regard to this document P21, it is not correct that the town was under the control of the HVO units. That is absolutely untrue. The town of Zenica could never have been under that control and that must be clear to one and all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, General, let us talk about what you did do, and I refer again to your testimony and the statement by Mr. Nobilo referring to the combat operations in Kuber. After you received this information that this combat contact had taken place as early as the 15th of April, you issued another order, and that is Exhibit number D269. If the witness could be given Exhibit D269. If we could also pull out D267 as well?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: These are Defence exhibits; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes. I apologise, Judge. They're Defence exhibits.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, after you received this information and you issued D269, you don't say anything about Kuber in this order, do you?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In this order I did not mention it, but I did in an oral order which I issued to the commander of the Vitez Brigade, Mr. Cerkez, at about 18.30, that the soldiers at Kuber should be informed that the movement of forces --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, General. We're talking about after 23.00. After you received your information at 23.00 and you issued this order, you did not include anything about Kuber in it, "Yes" or "No"?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In this order, no, but in the executive order that I issued at 18.30 the answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, General. You answered the question. Now, General, this order has the Vitez Brigade taking action at 5.30 in the morning. This action is in conjunction with the action of the military police who you have ordered, in Exhibit 267, to secure the road between Vitez and Busovaca; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know. Perhaps there was a mistake in the interpretation but this is an order issued to the Vitezovi and to the military police. Could you please repeat your question to me?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The question is that this order to the Vitez Brigade that has them performing a task at 5.30 in the morning, is supposed to be done --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Which one are you speaking about now? Are you speaking --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: 269. 269, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: 269. All right. Continue, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, that order contemplates the Vitez Brigade operating in conjunction with the military police who are taking over the road; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Point 2 of this order is written down, and that is a task according to the standards that I learned in the Yugoslav People's Army. This is a very precise assignment as to what should be done, that is to say, what the Vitez Brigade is supposed to do. In point number 2, I do not see the take-over of a road anywhere. The task issued to the Vitez Brigade in document 269 is written up very precisely. That is in point number 2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, in Exhibit 267, you have the military police ensuring that the road between Vitez and Busovaca is free and open; do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I do you recall that. That is a regular military police task, that is to say, the traffic police of the military police has this as a daily task, to ensure the road --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Please answer the question specifically. Try to be very specific, Mr. Kehoe. Try to bring out the two orders, to contrast them, the one of the 15th of April, which is 267, and the 16th of April, which is given at 1.30; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: General Blaskic, try to answer specifically when the questions are asked, and then afterwards, you can make comments. Please rephrase your question so that you can ask the question that you want to ask.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you, as the commander, want these two forces to operate in a coordinated fashion?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think that this task is quite clear to all. There has to be a certain degree of coordination so that there would not be mutual activity. But your question is not quite clear. Did I want them to operate in coordination? Well, of course. I didn't want to have any lack of coordination in terms of carrying out the tasks that they were ordered to do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Now, you noted for us during direct examination that combat activities ensued in the Lasva Valley at 05.30 in the morning. What time did you begin to use your artillery, General?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. Let me have a look at my notes. According to my notes, I was awakened by a detonation in the immediate vicinity of the Hotel Vitez itself at 5.00 in the morning or ten past five, approximately, but not at 5.30.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, let me help you out, at 9.45 in the morning, the artillery commander told you that he was ready for action; is that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At twenty-five minutes past nine, the commander of the artillery informed me that he was prepared for action at the request, that is to say, at the request.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then there was no firing prior to that time; is that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: There was firing. The Hotel Vitez was hit before that. Now who is firing? You tell me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me. Was your artillery firing prior to 9.25?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The artillery that I commanded did not open fire before 9.25.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, you had exclusive control over your artillery, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I had control over the artillery of the command of the Operative Zone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The artillery that was in part of the Operative Zone, there were artillery pieces in motion in the rock quarry, weren't there?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It included the artillery that was in the rock quarry, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me show you something, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I can begin with a map, I have smaller, individual copies as well. This is the exhibit you can show to the witness. You can put one on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The map will be referenced 689 and the reduced versions will be 689/1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, the area on the map that is designated with the yellow dot is the approximate area of the rock quarry where you had artillery pieces on the morning of the 16th; correct, General?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It is the area of Mali Mosunj, whereas the precise position of the artillery pieces is better known to the commander of the artillery. At one point in time, it was there, but whether it was there specifically on the 16th of April --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Approximately the area. It was approximately the area. Move to another question, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I can return to the milinfosum of the morning of the 16th of April, 1993, Mr. President. This is a military information summary, Mr. President, of the British Battalion of 16 April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is Prosecution Exhibit 690.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, with regard to this particular exhibit, I would like to turn to the second page, Mr. Usher, which has "Vitez." It says in the last sentence: "The main incidents are listed below: "A. At 0645 hours, an [unidentified] U/I field gun started to fire from the area of the hill feature centred on [grid reference] GR YJ 196945." Now, General, this particular field gun, according to the map to your left, has the grid reference of Mosunj, and it indicates that the British Battalion reports that your weapons were firing at 06.45 in the morning, and by "firing," I'm talking about your artillery. Now, that, General, is some three hours prior to you admitting that your HVO weaponry had begun to fire.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I did not look at all the requests, but the first time I got a request for firing was at 8.55. I do not believe that my artillery could have opened fire without a request from the commander of the Vitez Brigade, and the commander informed me that he was ready to fire at 9.25.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General --

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: And that is my answer to this question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, General, you are the one who told us on direct examination that you had exclusive control as to when that artillery battery fired; didn't you say that?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's right, I said control over the artillery that was under my command. I had a commander of the artillery -- the commander of the artillery was on the line, and at 9.25, he informed me on the 16th of April, 1993 that he was ready to fire. The artillery was aimed at the front line against the Serbs in the early morning hours of the 16th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you saying, General, that this particular individual fired without your authorisation at 06.45?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. I'm saying that at that time, I did not receive any request to open fire, and the artillery that is under my command did not receive orders to open any kind of fire before 09.25.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So given that you told us on page 18519 that "... nobody could issue," and this is at line 18, "... nobody could issue orders for artillery fire except myself," this person, according to your testimony, fired on positions without your authorisation; is that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. I already said that fire could not have been opened before 9.25 when the commander informed me that he was ready to open fire. Whether the artillery of the Operative Zone was specifically at that position or not, that, I'm not sure of because there were changes in firing positions. I have to explain here that the artillery pieces were aimed at the front line against the Serbs, that is to say, towards the Travnik front line, and a certain time had to pass before the artillery would turn in another direction and be relocated, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say it's directed towards the Serbs. Let us go down to the next insertion at 07.30. It's the same page, Mr. Usher. "B. There were a number of houses reported to be on fire in the predominantly Muslim village of Preocica, grid reference 2597. This was believed to be as a result of the serial A," i.e., the firing that was taking place as of 06.45 from Mosunj. So your artillery batteries, General, according to this military information summary are firing on Muslim villages in the early morning hours of the 16th of April, 1993 at the same time when Ahmici is being ransacked, burnt, and the citizens being murdered. Did you realise that that's happening at the same time?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In that information that you're reading out to me, it is not mentioned which artillery is in question, at least from what I heard. I said which artillery was under my command, and my answer is still that I could not issue an order to fire in that direction when the artillery was not ready before 9.15 -- sorry, 9.25. Twenty-five minutes past nine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's move down to (G) where we also focus on your artillery batteries, and we're talking about the same grid reference in Mosunj. In (G) it reflects a multi-barrelled rocket launcher, MBRL, fired two salvo's, one, of 12 rounds, the other, of 8 rounds, ten minutes later from the area of grid reference 196945. Now, that is your area. That is Mosunj, where you had artillery pieces; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, you are saying to me now that there was a MBRL, and you're talking about a gun within the span of two hours. It is illiterate, from a military point of view, to put in position these two different pieces. It was either a gun or a multiple barrelled rocket launcher. It was either/or, but not the both. Not both kinds of artillery pieces. So it is said that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honour, never according to the rules and according to the regulations governing --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: What rules?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The rules of the JNA on the combat use of artillery. Never are two of the same artillery pieces put on one in the same position because for practical reasons. If one discovered and destroyed, then the other one is deployed too. And the distance is over one kilometre, that is to say, one artillery piece from another artillery piece. Second, I would have to ask the following: Which MBRL, a 122-millimetre, multiple-barrelled rocket launcher I returned on the 8th of April, 1993? A multiple-barreled rocket launcher, 122 millimetres, the one that was under my command. And for a multiple-barreled rocket launcher that was 128 millimetres, we never had the missiles for that because the factory for the production of these projectiles was under the control of the army of Republika Srpska and not a single rocket could have been fired from it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: But, General, didn't we all see movie pictures of the Second World War with artillery pieces massed closing by each other and firing at the same time or am I mistaken?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honour, time did not allow me to explain about the artillery. We are equating different things here. The other day when we talked about Merdani, when the Prosecutor asked me about the artillery, everything is the artillery for us over here, you see, whereas artillerymen have a clear distinction between what the artillery is, the one that I command, and what is the artillery that each and every soldier has. There are multiple-barreled rocket launchers of 60 millimetres. That is what one soldier can carry and lose. Then there are rocket launchers of 82 millimetres, mortars that belong to infantry units, and I commanded an artillery that had larger calibres, and special vehicles are needed in order to move that, to relocate it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: You say that that was the position prescribed by JNA military regulations?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
